Review response fit and the support for uncertainty summaries

Source: R/api-estimation.R, R/api-methods.R, R/api-plotting-dispatch.R, and 1 more
diagnose_mfrm.Rd

Compute observation residuals, element/overall Infit and Outfit (MnSq and ZSTD), PTMEA, model/real SEs, facet separation/reliability/strata, fixed/random facet chi-square screens, inter-rater agreement, unexpected responses, fair averages, displacement, and optional marginal-fit or residual PCA diagnostics for an ordinary RSM/PCM or one-family GPCM fit_mfrm() object.

Usage

diagnose_mfrm(
  fit,
  interaction_pairs = NULL,
  top_n_interactions = 20,
  whexact = FALSE,
  fit_df_method = "facets",
  diagnostic_mode = c("both", "legacy", "marginal_fit"),
  residual_pca = c("none", "overall", "facet", "both"),
  pca_max_factors = 10L
)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_diagnostics'
summary(
  object,
  digits = 3,
  top_n = 10,
  detail = c("brief", "full"),
  include_person = FALSE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'mfrm_diagnostics'
plot(
  x,
  type = c("marginal_fit", "marginal_pairwise", "bubble", "residual_pca"),
  view = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

fit

Ordinary RSM, PCM, or one-family GPCM fit_mfrm() result (testlet, random-rater, corrected-JML, and two-family GPCM fits use mfrm_response_diagnostics()).

interaction_pairs

Optional list of length-two facet-name vectors to screen for pairwise residual interactions (NULL screens all non-Person facet pairs).

top_n_interactions

Maximum number of largest-magnitude interaction rows retained in the quick-preview table (20 default).

whexact

Logical or "legacy_linear" controlling the Wilson-Hilferty cube-root standardization for InfitZSTD and OutfitZSTD (FALSE = FACETS WHEXACT=YES with q/3 mean term; TRUE = WHEXACT=NO; "legacy_linear" = unadjusted linear Z).

fit_df_method

Standardization variance/df convention: "facets" (default; fourth-moment variance 2/q^2 with ZSTD capped at +/-9), "engine" (count-based df), or "both" (df < 1 or infinite-primary JML proxy rows withhold ZSTD).

diagnostic_mode

"both" (default: plug-in residual + posterior marginal category-count screens), "legacy", or "marginal_fit".

residual_pca

Exploratory residual PCA scope: "none" (default), "overall", "facet", or "both".

pca_max_factors

Maximum number of principal components extracted when residual_pca != "none" (10L default).

object

Output from diagnose_mfrm().

digits

Number of digits for printed numeric values.

top_n

Number of highest-absolute-Z fit rows to keep.

detail

Console detail: "brief" (default) prints the first-screen review; "full" prints the additional structured tables.

include_person

If TRUE, person-level identifiers may be printed in fit-review tables. The default keeps identifiers out of console output; person-level rows remain available in the returned object.

...

All views accept draw = FALSE, top_n, and preset. Marginal views accept facet; pairwise plots additionally accept metric = "exact" or "adjacent". Bubbles accept fit_stat ("Infit" or "Outfit"), bubble_size ("SE", "N", or "equal"), facets, include_person = FALSE, marginal = c("auto", "histogram", "none"), and the heuristic fit_range = c(0.5, 1.5). PCA accepts mode, facet, and component, as described in plot.mfrm_residual_pca(). Controls for other views are rejected.

x

An mfrm_diagnostics result from diagnose_mfrm().

type

"marginal_fit", "marginal_pairwise", "bubble", or "residual_pca".

view

For marginal fit, "std_residual" (default) or "prop_diff"; for bubbles, "measure" (default) or "infit_outfit"; for PCA, "scree", "parallel_scree", "parallel_excess", or "loadings". Omit it for "marginal_pairwise" and use metric instead.

Value

An mfrm_diagnostics object (calculation_version = 2L) containing obs, measures, overall_fit, fit, reliability, precision_profile, precision_review, parameter_uncertainty, facet_precision, facets_chisq, interactions, interrater, unexpected, fair_average, displacement, marginal_fit, residual_pca_*, fit_readiness*, and replay_inputs.

An object of class summary.mfrm_diagnostics with:

  • overview: design-level counts and residual-PCA mode

  • decision: the same plain-language fit-readiness decision used by summary(fit), retained ahead of diagnostic screening results

  • fit_readiness, fit_readiness_components, and fit_readiness_parameters: readiness provenance inherited from the source fit and retained separately from diagnostic-screening status

  • status: concise front-door status block for quick review

  • key_warnings: highest-priority warnings to review first

  • next_actions: recommended follow-up helpers

  • diagnostic_basis: guide to legacy versus strict diagnostic targets

  • fit_standardization: guide to the df convention used for fit ZSTD

  • overall_fit: global fit block

  • precision_profile: active precision tier and recommended use of the available uncertainty calculations

  • precision_review: separation / reliability / strata review for the sample- and population-basis modes (paired with precision_profile)

  • reliability: facet-level separation/reliability summary

  • facets_chisq: facets-style fixed-effect chi-square heterogeneity screen across non-person facets

  • interrater: inter-rater agreement / pairwise correlation / rater separation overview when a Rater facet is present

  • misfit_flagged: rows flagged by the Infit / Outfit mean-square band

  • fit_screening: counts of all, classified and unclassified elements for the mean-square band and each ZSTD cutoff. Either available statistic crossing a cutoff flags the element; otherwise a missing statistic leaves it unclassified. Rates require every element to be classified. Nonfinite statistics and negative mean squares are unavailable, not passing values.

  • misfit_thresholds: named numeric vector with the misfit lower / upper thresholds used to populate misfit_flagged

  • category_usage: per-category response-frequency summary used to flag empty / collapsed categories

  • top_fit: top maximum |ZSTD| rows with both statistics available

  • marginal_coverage: classified, unclassified and flagged category cells, groups and level pairs; counts of available flags do not describe missing results

  • marginal_fit: optional strict marginal-fit overview when requested

  • top_marginal_cells: largest strict marginal residual cells when requested

  • marginal_pairwise: optional strict pairwise local-dependence overview

  • top_marginal_pairs: largest strict pairwise residual summaries

  • marginal_guidance: interpretation labels for strict marginal diagnostics

  • reporting_map: manuscript-oriented guide to what is covered here versus which companion outputs should be consulted

  • flags: compact flag counts for major diagnostics

  • notes: short interpretation notes

  • digits: numeric-print precision threaded through to print.summary.mfrm_diagnostics()

For plot(): Invisibly, a ggplot object. Use plot_data() to inspect its tables and notes. The plot does not add unavailable diagnostics or qualify intervals.

Details

Fit, SE, and separation conventions. MML residuals plug in Person EAPs; legacy JML residuals use optimizer coordinates (PersonMeasureBasis; variances <= 1e-10 withhold standardized residuals, and any unavailable contributing row sets element MnSq/df to NA via FitStatus/FitReason). RealSE = ModelSE * sqrt(max(Infit, 1)) inflates ModelSE for underfit (Fixed = TRUE anchors keep NA SEs and suppress aggregate facet reliability). Wright and Masters (1982) separation indices use sample SD (n - 1) and RMSE across finite free levels (TrueSD = sqrt(max(SD^2 - RMSE^2, 0)), \(G = \mathrm{TrueSD}/\mathrm{RMSE}\), \(R = G^2/(1 + G^2)\), \(H = (4G + 1)/3\)); rater separation measures severity spread rather than inter-rater agreement.

Read decision and key_warnings, then use the tables below to locate results needing investigation. The summary reuses diagnostics; it does not refit or promote a restricted source fit to inferential use.

plot() method: Plot saved ordinary-model diagnostics

Inspect an existing diagnostic result to locate cells or elements needing follow-up. The selected display retains unavailable results and screening limits.

Interpreting results

  • Infit/Outfit have model-reference value 1. Values above 1 describe excess residual variation; values below 1 describe greater predictability. InfitZSTD/OutfitZSTD standardize those mean squares; they are not effect sizes or calibrated tests after fitting and repeated screening. top_fit ranks only rows with both ZSTD values available. Its absence of a level does not establish acceptable fit; inspect object$fit and FitReason for unavailable standardizations.

  • Reliability/Separation describe how spread out facet measures are relative to their estimated error. RealReliability/RealSeparation use fit-inflated SEs, not lower confidence limits. High rater separation can indicate severity differences, not agreement. Read ReliabilityBasis, ReliabilityUse and the computation details in diagnose_mfrm().

  • fit_screening distinguishes classified from unclassified elements. A known cutoff crossing remains flagged if another statistic is missing; missing evidence is not a pass. Flags guide review, not automatic deletion.

  • diagnostic_basis distinguishes EAP plug-in response residuals from posterior-integrated category-count screens. They answer different fit questions; neither label alone authorizes a hypothesis test.

  • In overview, Observations counts retained rating rows and Persons counts respondents. Repeated ratings of one Person do not create additional independent Persons.

Choosing a view

For plot():

Marginal fit and pairwise plots require strict marginal diagnostics from diagnose_mfrm() with diagnostic_mode = "both" or "marginal_fit" for supported MML RSM/PCM models. Positive residuals indicate more observed category usage or agreement than expected; negative values indicate less. Returned full_table and retention distinguish omitted and unavailable rows. A flag is a descriptive review rule, not a calibrated test.

Bubble plots place measures against mean-square fit, or Infit against Outfit. Bubble size can represent SE or observation count; neither a review band nor bubble size alone justifies deleting an element.

The PCA convenience route can derive PCA from the diagnostic result. For repeated PCA displays, first save analyze_residual_pca() and use its plot() method. Parallel-reference generation remains an analysis step.

Expected point-measure correlation under ordinary JML

For ordinary additive RSM/PCM JML without group-mean anchors, measures$PTMEAExpected adds a conditional reference beside observed PTMEA. Let x be the oriented generating measure, e the expected score, v its conditional model variance, and N the sum of frequency weights within the element. The reference is $$\frac{\operatorname{Cov}_w(x,e)}{ \sqrt{\operatorname{Var}_w(x)\{\operatorname{Var}_w(e)+(N-2)\bar v_w/N\}}}.$$ Weighted moments use the same observations and normalized frequency weights. PTMEAExpectedAsymptotic omits the (N-2)/N adjustment. The correction is Linacre's published finite-count reporting approximation; it is not an exact expectation of the sample correlation, a significance test or a confidence interval. Calibration is held fixed. Different administered PCM scales are retained when calculating each observation's expectation and variance.

PTMEAExpectedN, PTMEAExpectedFactor, PTMEAExpectedStatus and PTMEAExpectedReason identify the calculation and unavailable states. At N = 2 the variance term vanishes; this does not establish perfect measurement or fit. Below N = 2, the corrected reference is unavailable (FACETS 4.5.0 can instead display a boundary value). The asymptotic reference remains available if its moments exist. Arbitrarily normalizing weights changes the corrected reference: use replication semantics for comparison. Constant predictors, invalid moments, or observations involving unanchored extreme main effects withhold the complete element's expected reference; they are not silently dropped. Fixed finite anchors remain usable.

FACETS 4.5.0 fixed-calibration PCM checks cover missing assignments and unit, integer, fractional and unequal replication weights. These checks establish a reporting convention within that scope, not general diagnostic calibration. Observed PTMEA retains its existing definition. MML, corrected JML, GPCM, fitted interactions and group-mean anchors do not receive the new expected-correlation columns. Recreate older diagnostics from the saved fit to obtain them; old saved results are not relabeled or silently recalculated. See Linacre (2008), The Expected Value of a Point-Biserial (or Similar) Correlation, Rasch Measurement Transactions, 22:1, 1154, including its later finite-count note: https://www.rasch.org/rmt/rmt221e.htm.

References

Linacre, J. M. (1989). Many-Facet Rasch Measurement. MESA Press.

Wright, B. D., & Masters, G. N. (1982). Rating scale analysis. MESA Press.

Wright, B. D., & Linacre, J. M. (1994). Reasonable mean-square fit values. Rasch Measurement Transactions, 8(3), 370.

Linacre, J. M. (2002). What do Infit and Outfit, Mean-square and Standardized mean? Rasch Measurement Transactions, 16(2), 878. https://www.rasch.org/rmt/rmt162f.htm

Yen, W. M. (1984). Effects of local item dependence on the fit and equating performance of the three-parameter logistic model. Applied Psychological Measurement, 8(2), 125–145. doi:10.1177/014662168400800201

Linacre, J. M. (2026). A user's guide to Facets Rasch-model computer programs. Winsteps.com.

Examples

# Long-running workflow; run explicitly when needed.
# example("diagnose_mfrm", run.dontrun = TRUE)
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Load the package and example ratings
library(mfrmr)
ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_operational")

# Fit the model
fit <- fit_mfrm(
  data = ratings,
  person = "Person",
  facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"),
  score = "Score",
  rating_min = 1, rating_max = 4, category_policy = "preserve",
  method = "MML",
  model = "RSM"
)

# Check model fit and the support for standard errors and intervals
diagnostics <- diagnose_mfrm(fit)
diagnostic_summary <- summary(diagnostics)
diagnostic_summary$decision

diagnostic_summary$key_warnings # Issues to investigate, if present
diagnostic_summary$top_fit      # Most unusual residual-based fit statistics

# Distinguish residual-based checks from marginal model checks
diagnostic_summary$diagnostic_basis[, c("DiagnosticPath", "Status", "Basis")]

# Check each residual's basis and the coverage of aggregate fit statistics
head(diagnostics$obs[, c("PersonMeasureBasis", "ConditionalVariance",
  "PearsonAvailable", "ResponseReason")])
diagnostics$overall_fit[, c("Infit", "Outfit", "FitUnavailableRows", "FitReason")]
} # }
library(mfrmr)

# Saved synthetic MML/RSM analysis of example_operational.
# For your own data, fit a model first; see ?fit_mfrm.
example_fit <- readRDS(system.file("examples", "operational-mml.rds", package = "mfrmr"))
fit <- example_fit$fit

# Check model fit and the support for standard errors and intervals
diagnostics <- example_fit$diagnostics
diagnostic_summary <- summary(diagnostics)
